title: Static manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC): two residual streams with Sinkhorn doubly-stochastic mixing, on the 081 incumbent
description: Robbie's 'deepseek hypermanifolds' architecture lead (no backlog P-ID; closest are P09/P10 learned residual gates/reinjection): replace the single residual stream with 2 streams joined around every attention and MLP sublayer by static DeepSeek mHC hyper-connections (learned sigmoid read/write weights, Sinkhorn-projected doubly stochastic stream mixing), initialized to be exactly the 081 network. Separate streams give the 5-layer model a learned alternative to one shared residual, e.g. keeping earlier proof-state features in one stream while later sublayers write to another, which should give expert iteration a more compositional starting point.
hypothesis: With one residual stream every sublayer reads the sum of all earlier writes; hyper-connections let the network learn per-sublayer read and write weights over separate streams and how much the streams exchange, a learned depth-connectivity that HC/mHC report improves pretraining at larger scale. The doubly stochastic mix keeps the stream mean a convex combination, so signal scale stays controlled (mHC's stability argument) through pretraining and the AdamW RL stage. If short-horizon training here is limited by interference between features in the shared residual, the model should solve more long (>=7) proofs after RL. Costs: ~10-15% fewer pretraining steps from the extra fp32 residual traffic (2x residual tensor), and the 80 logits start at the identity-equivalent point and move at AdamW lr 1e-3, so the learned connectivity may stay close to the baseline (a null result).
expected_delta: -40 to +20 theorems at >=7 (3-seed mean vs 404; most likely a small loss from fewer steps)

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) subclassed as HyperGPT: same blocks/weights, forward rewritten for 2 residual streams joined by static mHC hyper-connections
arch.change: CHANGED versus 081-claude: static manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC, DeepSeek-AI 2025, arXiv 2512.24880; Hyper-Connections, Zhu et al. 2024) with expansion rate n=2. The embedding is copied into 2 residual streams (B,T,2,256). Around each of the 10 sublayers (attention, MLP of 5 blocks) a HyperConnection reads h = sigmoid(read_logits) @ streams, applies the unchanged fork sublayer (ln1+attn or ln2+fc1/gelu/fc2) to h, and updates streams <- Sinkhorn(exp(mix_logits)) @ streams + 2*sigmoid(write_logits) (x) out. Sinkhorn-Knopp: 20 row/column normalization iterations (doubly stochastic, mHC's manifold). Readout: head(ln_f(mean over streams)). Static only: no input-dependent (dynamic) mappings. Init: read_logits +4 on stream (sublayer index mod 2), -4 on the other (weights 0.982/0.018, sum exactly 1); write_logits 0 (weight 1); mix_logits 4*I (mix ~[[0.982,0.018],[0.018,0.982]]). With identical streams at init this is exactly the fork residual block (CPU check: logits differ from the base GPT with the same weights by 2.4e-7). All residual-stream arithmetic (read, mix, write) runs in fp32 with autocast disabled; sublayers still run in bf16 autocast.
arch.n_params_detail: 081's 4,000,000 plus 10 HyperConnections x (2 read + 2 write + 4 mix logits) = 80 -> 4,000,080. Hyper-connection params live in model.hc (not model.blocks) and persist into RL, where the harness AdamW trains them with everything else.
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: HyperGPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) in pretrain.py (GPT subclass); state dict = fork GPT keys plus hc.0-hc.9.{read,write,mix}_logits. The fork's GPT(**cfg) alone cannot rebuild it.
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per block (5 per sample), used by the unchanged fork attention; hyper-connections are per-token and need no cache. CPU check: incremental cached decode matches full forward to 3e-7 with perturbed hyper-connection params; fork sample.generate_ids runs.

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial); hyper-connection logits in a second AdamW group (same lr/betas/schedule, weight decay 0)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: unchanged from 081-claude: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: unchanged from 081-claude: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: unchanged from 081-claude: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: HyperGPT weights (fork GPT weights plus the 80 hyper-connection logits); pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW over all parameters
optimizer.hyper_connection_group: AdamW lr 1e-3 (same warmup/cosine as the auxiliary group), betas (0.9, 0.95), weight_decay 0.0 so decay does not drag reads/mixes toward uniform; included in the global grad-norm clip 1.0

config.init: Exactly 070-claude (same as 069-claude): fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 070-claude. Hyper-connections (new): read_logits +4/-4, write_logits 0, mix_logits 4*I (identity-equivalent network at init).
